section_summary: The section begins with consular reports on Japan’s increasing control of merchant shipping in 1940–41, including freight pooling, vessel allocation, and plans for centralized state management. Later documents address wartime shipping shortages and salvage, a lengthy inquiry into cargo discharged from the Sanyo Maru at New York, and the treatment of visiting Japanese naval vessels under U.S. customs rules.

subfiles.title: Japan Shipping Promotion Society report, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Describes the new Japan Shipping Promotion Society and its proposed funding.
subfiles.summary: The Communications Ministry and major shipowners and builders organized a society for shipping and shipbuilding research and subsidies, with Murata as president.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during December 1940
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports proposed shipping legislation, administrative reorganization, and freight pooling.
subfiles.summary: The Communications Ministry planned a bill expanding its control of shipping firms, routes, construction, and finances. Its Shipping Control Bureau might become a board. The report outlines a proposed pool accounting system for freight revenues and operating costs.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during January 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Traces Japanese shipping controls and disputes over joint freight accounting.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the Central Control Transportation Association’s organization and the assignment of carrier groups to operating blocs. It explains delays and opposition to fixed charter rates and pooled freight accounts.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during February 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Covers proposals for unified shipping control, opposition to pooling, and a shipping protection bill.
subfiles.summary: Officials considered a central maritime authority covering transportation and shipbuilding. Murata opposed the proposed joint freight account. The government convened shipping interests, while a bill proposed naval powers over merchant vessel movements in wartime.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during April 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports ship allocation and the start of joint freight accounting.
subfiles.summary: The Central Marine Transportation Control Association coordinated carriers and commodity shippers, incorporating sailing vessels into near seas transport. The joint accounting system began April 1 and prioritized petroleum, rice, salt, and coal while reducing other allocations.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during May 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Describes a proposed marine transportation ordinance and cargo allocation problems.
subfiles.summary: A proposed ordinance would expand ministry control of shipping firms, routes, and finances. The control association struggled to move essential commodities amid vessel shortages, military requisitioning, and complaints from textile producers.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during July 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports plans for fuller national control and reduced shipping allocations.
subfiles.summary: The government considered chartering and assigning all ships through a strengthened central association, appointing marine commissioners at ports, and further cutting cargo space allocations.

subfiles.title: Shipping in the Japanese Empire during August 1941
subfiles.from: Roy M. Melbourne, American Vice Consul, Kobe
subfiles.about: Examines Japan’s announced plan for state control and management of shipping.
subfiles.summary: Japan announced a single authority for shipping, seamen, and shipbuilding under the National General Mobilisation Law. The report discusses whether government officials or established firms would operate vessels, expected mergers and reduced profits, and doubts about administrative efficiency.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of Sanyo Maru cargo inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a Netherlands inquiry about Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: Treasury awaits an expedited report from the New York customs collector.

subfiles.title: Treasury letter withholding Sanyo Maru cargo data
subfiles.about: Explains why requested cargo information cannot yet be released.
subfiles.summary: Treasury has the data but seeks proof that the Netherlands committee is entitled to confidential customs information.

subfiles.title: Copy of Treasury letter on confidential cargo data
subfiles.about: Duplicates Treasury’s explanation for withholding Sanyo Maru cargo data.
subfiles.summary: Release awaits evidence of the Netherlands committee’s interest in the cargo.

subfiles.title: State Department note requesting clarification of Netherlands interest
subfiles.about: Requests details of the Netherlands committee’s interest in Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: Customs has obtained the information but requires grounds for releasing confidential records.

subfiles.title: State Department forwarding note to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the Netherlands Ambassador’s explanation of the committee’s interest.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the ambassador’s December 17 note about Sanyo Maru cargo.

subfiles.title: Netherlands request to expedite cargo decision
subfiles.about: Asks U.S. authorities to expedite the Sanyo Maru cargo inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador requests renewed State Department assistance in obtaining a decision.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese shipping shortages in Asia
subfiles.about: Relays reports on salvage, wooden vessels, Hong Kong transshipment, and vessel registration.
subfiles.summary: Chinese information describes Japanese salvage efforts, construction of wooden vessels at Saigon, use of Hong Kong as a transshipment hub, and new controls over smaller vessels in the Philippines and Java.

subfiles.title: Netherlands committee’s custodial authority over Sanyo Maru cargo
subfiles.about: Explains the committee’s legal interest in Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: The committee acts as custodian under authority from the Netherlands government in London.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese rail freight and shipping
subfiles.about: Relays Chinese reports on freight trains and Japanese coastal vessels.
subfiles.summary: Reports daily trains to Manchuria and Japanese construction of sail and wooden vessels to ease shipping shortages.

subfiles.title: Treasury release of Sanyo Maru customs report
subfiles.about: Provides the customs report after the Netherlands committee establishes custodial authority.
subfiles.summary: Treasury encloses a New York customs report on the cargo’s disposition.

subfiles.title: Copy of Treasury release letter
subfiles.about: Duplicates Treasury’s letter enclosing the customs report.
subfiles.summary: The committee’s custodial status permits release of the cargo report.

subfiles.title: Customs agent report on Sanyo Maru cargo
subfiles.from: Cosimo Analli, Customs Agent, New York
subfiles.about: Traces listed Sanyo Maru cargo items after discharge in New York.
subfiles.summary: The report identifies import entries, sales, exports back to Japan, remittances, and stored Japanese oak. It records values and destinations for the manifest’s exhibits.

subfiles.title: State Department account of Sanyo Maru cargo disposition
subfiles.about: Transmits detailed customs findings on Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: The note reproduces the customs agent’s itemized account of goods sold, reexported, or stored, including values and proceeds.

subfiles.title: Netherlands follow-up on two cargo sale lots
subfiles.about: Requests seizure details and proceeds for two Sanyo Maru cargo sale lots.
subfiles.summary: The committee seeks the quantity seized and the distribution of proceeds from lots 576 and 569.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment of follow-up inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request for more cargo information.
subfiles.summary: The inquiry has been referred to the appropriate U.S. authorities.

subfiles.title: State Department referral of follow-up inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards the Netherlands request for details on two cargo items.
subfiles.summary: State asks Treasury to provide available information.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of follow-up inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request for further customs information.
subfiles.summary: Treasury will obtain a report from the New York collector.

subfiles.title: Treasury forwarding letter on cargo sale lots
subfiles.about: Forwards the collector’s report on disputed Sanyo Maru cargo items.
subfiles.summary: Treasury encloses the New York collector’s findings.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on cargo sale lots
subfiles.about: Provides sale and seizure figures for lots 576 and 569.
subfiles.summary: The note relays the collector’s description of the merchandise and distribution of sale proceeds.

subfiles.title: Collector’s report on Sanyo Maru sale lots
subfiles.from: T. J. Hogue, Acting Assistant Collector
subfiles.about: Details merchandise and accounting for lots 576 and 569.
subfiles.summary: The report lists buttons, socks, seized slide fasteners, smokers’ articles, rubber goods, and sale expenses.

subfiles.title: Law firm inquiry about requisitioned NYK vessels
subfiles.about: Seeks evidence of Japanese government control or diversion of NYK ships before Pearl Harbor.
subfiles.summary: Admiralty counsel asks whether requisition or orders to return to Japan affected cargo claims against NYK’s bankruptcy trustee.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Japanese vessel diversions
subfiles.from: Green H. Hackworth, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes available reports on requisitioned or diverted Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy could not establish definitive requisition records but named several reportedly affected vessels. It described controls exercised through the Central Marine Transportation Control Association and the Ships Protection Law.

subfiles.title: Netherlands inquiry about missing toy cases
subfiles.about: Questions why three cases of toys disappeared from the later account of lot 576.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador seeks clarification of whether the toys were included with other merchandise in lot 576.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of toy inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the renewed inquiry about Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: Treasury will seek clarification from New York customs.

subfiles.title: Copy of Treasury acknowledgment of toy inquiry
subfiles.about: Duplicates Treasury’s acknowledgment of the cargo question.
subfiles.summary: A New York customs response is pending.

subfiles.title: State Department referral of toy inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks Treasury to clarify the discrepancy concerning Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the ambassador’s July 2 note.

subfiles.title: Treasury forwarding letter resolving cargo discrepancy
subfiles.about: Forwards the collector’s clarification of the disputed cargo items.
subfiles.summary: Treasury encloses the New York collector’s report.

subfiles.title: Collector’s correction of Sanyo Maru lot number
subfiles.about: Corrects the identification of three cases manifested as toys.
subfiles.summary: The goods were appraised as combs and sold in lot 572; lot 576 contained different goods.

subfiles.title: State Department correction to Netherlands Ambassador
subfiles.about: Relays the corrected customs identification and sale lot.
subfiles.summary: The three cases listed as toys were combs sold in lot 572, separate from lot 576.

subfiles.title: Telegram on losses and salvage near China
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese ship sinking, Conte Verde salvage, and increased use of wooden craft.
subfiles.summary: Chinese intelligence reports salvage at Shanghai and growing reliance on junks and railways for cargo transport.

subfiles.title: Embassy transmittal of article on Japan’s shipping shortage
subfiles.from: Howard Bucknell, Counselor of Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Forwards Gunther Stein’s newspaper article on Japan’s shipping shortage.
subfiles.summary: The cover letter highlights the article’s account of worsening transport constraints.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Shipping Shortage
subfiles.about: Analyzes shipping constraints on Japan’s occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: Stein describes development projects, wooden shipbuilding, administrative conflict, and mounting supply problems across occupied Asia. He argues that Allied attacks and scarce shipping undermine exchange between Japan and its occupied territories.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japanese merchant fleet estimates
subfiles.about: Relays press claims about Japanese shipping needs, fleet size, and shipbuilding.
subfiles.summary: A German newspaper reports Japanese tonnage estimates and construction of wooden ships in Southeast Asia.

subfiles.title: Chungking despatch on salvage of Italian vessels
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, American Ambassador, Chungking
subfiles.about: Forwards a report on Japanese salvage of Italian vessels at Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Gauss reports that Lepanto had been raised and efforts continued on Conte Verde.

subfiles.title: Salvage of Italian vessels at Shanghai
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, Second Secretary on detail at Sian
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese salvage of the scuttled Lepanto and Conte Verde.
subfiles.summary: Lepanto was reportedly raised; workers were trying to right Conte Verde in the Whangpoo River.

subfiles.title: Forwarding of Italian vessel salvage despatch
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Algiers
subfiles.about: Directs transmission of the Shanghai salvage report to Allied officials concerned with Italy.
subfiles.summary: The mission should pass the report to Mr. Reber for possible use by the Italian government.

subfiles.title: Counselor’s memorandum on Japanese vessel visits
subfiles.about: Records discussions of proposed visits by three Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Savage says the visits were approved with usual courtesies and Commerce could be informed accordingly.

subfiles.title: Commerce memorandum on customs treatment of Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.from: Acting Assistant Director, Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on customs entry, clearance, and export declarations for Japanese naval vessels.
subfiles.summary: Two naval tankers and a cargo vessel were expected at San Francisco. Commerce asks whether their oil loading and imported printed matter require entry, clearance, manifests, or export declarations under the Tariff Act.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Commerce memorandum on Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.from: Acting Assistant Director, Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation
subfiles.about: Duplicates the request for guidance on Japanese naval vessels and customs formalities.
subfiles.summary: Commerce seeks State’s view on entry, clearance, and oil export declarations.
